Nature rebelled against this condition and brought forth the most manifold reactions, such as the rise of many robber bands, of many Messiahs, the Judaism of the Pharisees made stricter and more monastic, the union of freedom and politics with it in Sadducaeism, the brotherly eremitic life of the Essenes, free from the passions and cares of their people, the brightening of Judaism through fairer blossoms of the deeper human nature in Platonism, finally the rising up and open preaching of John to all the people - and last the appearance of Jesus, who attacked the evil of his people at the root, namely at its haughty and hostile setting-apart from all nations, and thus wanted to lead it to the God of all men, to universal love of men, to the renunciation of the loveless and spiritless mechanism of their divine service, whose new teaching for that very reason became even more the religion of the world than of his people - a proof of how deeply he had grasped the needs of his age and how the Jews were sunk in a salvationless absence of the good and in the fury of spiritual servitude.
zh: 犹太民族绝对厌恶、鄙视周围所有的民族，它只想为自己、高高在上地、单独守在自己的种类、自己的习俗、自己的自负里；任何与他人平起平坐、通过习俗达成的结合，在它眼里都是令人憎恶的丑事，可它又由于自己小国所处的位置、由于商业往来、由于罗马人促成的各民族的结合，与别的民族处在多种多样的关系里；各民族要结合起来的冲动，必然让犹太人那种孤立自己的癖好败下阵来，而在那些斗争之后——这民族越独特，斗争就越可怕——它也真的败下阵来，并且因为国家被交到一种外来势力手里，深受伤害、满腔怨恨。
此后这民族更加顽固地死守它那些律法条文式的宗教诫命；它把自己的立法直接追溯到一位排他性的上帝；在它的宗教里，做无数没有意义、没有含义的动作是本质性的，而这民族迂腐奴性的精神，连日常生活里最无关紧要的举动都给规定了规则，让整个民族看去像一个修士会——对上帝和美德的事奉，就是死板套话底下一种强制的生活，留给精神的，只有一种顽固的骄傲：为自己这份服从而骄傲，那是奴隶对并非自己给自己订的法律的服从。
可是这种顽固，挡不住它那沉重命运的坠落越来越快，而一天天有更多的重量挂到这命运上去。
这整体已经一次性地、永远地撕碎了。
它那种隔离的狂热，抵挡不住政治上的依附，也抵挡不住与外人结合带来的影响。
犹太民族的这种处境，必然在质地更好的人身上唤醒一种需要：他们无法否认自己的自我感受，也无法把自己压低成死机器，同时又压低成奴性的狂怒；他们需要更自由的活动和更纯粹的独立，而不是带着修士般的忙碌、跟着一套没有精神、没有本质的琐碎惯例的机械活动，去过一种没有自我意识的日子；他们需要更高贵的享受，而不是在这门奴隶的活计里自以为大、并为它发狂。

自然起来反抗这种处境，逼出形形色色的反应，比如许多强盗团伙、许多弥赛亚的出现，法利赛人把犹太教弄得更严厉、更像修士，撒都该派把自由和政治与它结合起来，艾赛尼派那种兄弟般的、摆脱了本民族激情和忧虑的隐修生活，柏拉图主义以更深的人性开出的更美的花朵照亮了犹太教，最后还有约翰向全体民众奋起公开布道——最后是耶稣的出现，他从根子上攻击自己民族的祸害，也就是攻击它那种傲慢而满怀敌意地把所有民族排除在外的做法，因此想把它引向所有人的上帝，引向普遍的人类之爱，引向放弃他们礼拜中那套没有爱、没有精神的机械活动，而他的新学说正因为如此，才更多地成了世界的宗教，而不是他民族的宗教——这证明他多么深地抓住了自己时代的需求，也证明犹太人已经沉入无可救药的善的缺席和精神受奴役的狂怒之中。

en: How the education of Jesus ripened - on this interesting question no reports at all have come down to us; only in his manly age does he appear, free from the Jewish sense, free from the narrow indolence that spends its only activity on the common needs and conveniences of life, as from ambition and other passions whose satisfactions would have forced him to enter into the contract of prejudices and vices.

His whole manner has the appearance that he was indeed brought up among his people, but far from it - and probably for longer than forty days - was animated by the enthusiasm of the reformer; at the same time, however, his way of acting and speaking bears in itself no traces of any education of another people or religion existing at that time.

He appears at once in a youthful way, with all the joyful hope and undoubting confidence of success; the resistance that comes to him from the deep-rooted prejudices of his people seems unexpected to him; the killed spirit of free religiosity, the stubborn frenzy of the slavish sense of his nation, he seemed to have forgotten.

By simple talk, by preaching to a great crowd while wandering about, he intends to turn the heart of his obstinate people; he holds the twelve friends, who have not long been acquainted with him, capable of producing this effect; he holds his nation ripe to be stirred and changed by such a sending out of such immature men, who in the sequel laid themselves open so often and who could presumably only repeat the words of Jesus.
Only through the bitter experience of the fruitlessness of his efforts does the youthful unconstrainedness die out, and he speaks with bitter violence, with a mind provoked by hostile resistance.
zh: 耶稣的教养是怎样成熟起来的，关于这个有趣的问题，根本没有半点消息传到我们这里；他直到成年的年纪才出场，摆脱了犹太人的心性，摆脱了那种狭隘的懒惰——它把唯一的活动花在生活里平庸的需要和舒适上——也摆脱了野心和别的激情，这些激情一旦得到满足，就会逼他去签下偏见和恶习的契约。
他的整个作风给人的印象是：他固然是在自己民族中间长大的，却远离这民族——大概还不止四十天——被改革者的热情所鼓舞；但与此同时，他行事和说话的方式，本身并不带当时任何一个别的民族或宗教的教养的痕迹。
他一出场就是年轻人的样子，带着一切快乐的希望和对成功毫不怀疑的信心；他自己民族那些根深蒂固的偏见给他的抵抗，在他看来是出乎意料的；那被扼杀的自由宗教性的精神，他那民族奴性的顽固狂热，他好像已经忘掉了。
他想靠简单的讲话、靠四处奔走时向一大群人布道，让他那冥顽不化的民族回心转意；他以为那十二个朋友——他们跟他相识还不久——有能力产生这种效果；他以为自己的民族已经成熟，凭这样派出这样一些不成熟的人就能被鼓动起来、被改变，而这些人后来还露出那么多破绽，大概也只能够学舌般地重复耶稣的话。
直到尝到自己的努力毫无结果的痛苦经验，那种年轻人的无所拘束才熄灭下去，他说话就带着痛苦的激烈，带着一颗被敌意的抵抗激怒的心。

en: What the Jews hoped from the future, the perfection of the theocracy, a kingdom of God - of that Jesus said to them: it has come, it is present; through faith in it it becomes actual and everyone a citizen of it.
With the peasant pride of the Jews there was necessarily bound up the feeling of their nullity, which through the slavery under their laws they had eternally to give themselves.

That they, that the son of a carpenter, should be capable of being members of the kingdom of God in their wretched actuality - to believe this, to give them this self-feeling, was the single and certainly difficult task; freedom from the yoke of the law [was] the negative character of that faith.

Jesus therefore attacks everywhere the dead mechanism of their religious life; the Jewish law had so corrupted itself that even for its excellent parts a mass of evasions, of ways of going around it, had been invented.

Jesus was indeed able to do little against the united power of an ingrained national pride, of the hypocrisy and sanctimoniousness interwoven with the whole constitution, and of the rule of the people's leaders founded thereon.

Jesus had the grief of seeing that his zeal to bring freedom and morality into the religiosity of his nation failed completely, that even his efforts, at least in a few men, to kindle better hopes and a better faith, by training them through more intimate intercourse for themselves and for the support of his efforts, had had a very ambiguous and incomplete effect (Matt.
20, 20, an incident that occurred after some years of intercourse of John and James with Jesus; - Judas.

Even in the last moments of his stay on earth, a few moments before his so-called ascension, they still showed the Jewish hope in its full greatness, that he would restore the state of the Israelites, Acts.
Jesus himself became a sacrifice of the hatred of the priesthood breaking out against him and of the wounded national vanity of his people.
zh: 犹太人指望从未来得到的东西，神权政治的完满，一个上帝之国——关于这个，耶稣对他们说：它已经来了，它就在眼前；凭着对这事的信仰，它就变成现实的，每个人都是它的公民。
与犹太人那种乡巴佬式的傲慢必然连在一起的，是对自己毫无价值的感受，而这种感受，他们由于处在自己法律的奴役之下，必须永远给自己。
他们，一个木匠的儿子，竟然能够在他们可悲的现实里做上帝之国的成员——要相信这一点，要给他们这种自我感受，这是唯一而确实艰难的任务；摆脱法律的枷锁，就是那种信仰的否定性特征。
所以耶稣到处攻击他们宗教生活里那套死板的机械活动；犹太法律已经败坏到这种地步：就连它那些出色的地方，人们也发明了一大堆推脱和绕开的办法。
耶稣确实无力对抗一种联合起来的力量，那就是根深蒂固的民族骄傲、与整个宪制缠在一起的伪善和假虔诚，以及建立在这上面的民众领袖的统治。
耶稣不得不痛心地看到，他要把自由和道德带进自己民族的宗教性里的那股热忱，彻底失败了；就连他那些努力——至少在少数人身上点燃更好的希望和更好的信仰，靠更亲密的交往把他们培养得能自立、也能支持他的努力——也只产生了十分含糊、十分不完整的效果（《马太福音》
20，20，这件事发生在约翰和雅各跟耶稣交往了几年之后；——犹大。
甚至在他留在世上的最后片刻，就在他所谓的升天前的片刻，他们还表现出那种犹太希望的全部伟大，说他会把以色列人的国家重新建立起来，《使徒行传》
耶稣自己也成了祭司阶层对他爆发出来的仇恨、以及他那民族受了伤害的民族虚荣的牺牲品。

en: It is very natural to expect that the new teaching of Jesus, received by Jewish heads, however free it was in itself and only the more polemical, had to be transformed into something positive, that out of it they would, come what might, create something they could slavishly serve.

The religion that Jesus bore within himself, one sees, was free of the spirit of his people; what occurs in his utterances that savours of superstition, e.g. the dominion of the demons over men, has by one part been cried out as terribly senseless, by others it was to be made good through the concepts of accommodation, time-ideas and the like; what must be said by us about such things that are to be regarded as superstition is that it does not belong to religion.
Otherwise Jesus's soul was free, independent of contingencies, [was] love of God and of the neighbour, to be holy as God is, the single necessary thing.

This religious purity is in a Jew certainly most admirable; his followers, by contrast, we see indeed renounce Jewish contingencies, but not purified from the spirit of dependence on such things in general; out of the discourses, out of what happened to Jesus in his own person, they soon create for themselves rules, commandments of duty, and free imitation of their teacher passes over into slavish service toward the master.
zh: 很自然可以预料，耶稣的新学说一旦被犹太人的脑袋接受，无论它本身多么自由、多么只是论战性的，都必然会变成某种实证的东西；无论事情怎样发展，他们都会从中给自己造出一样可以奴性侍奉的东西。
可以看出，耶稣心里怀有的宗教，不沾他民族的精神；他那些话里出现的、带迷信味道的东西，比如魔鬼对人的统治，被一部分人痛斥为极其荒唐，另一部分人则想用迁就、时代观念之类的概念把它圆过去；至于我们对着这类该看作迷信的东西必须说的话，那就是：它不属于宗教。
除此之外，耶稣的灵魂是自由的，不依赖种种偶然；爱上帝和爱邻人，像上帝那样圣洁，是唯一必要的事。
这种宗教上的纯净，在一个犹太人身上确实最值得惊叹；可是他的追随者，我们看见他们固然放弃了犹太人的种种偶然，却没有从依赖这类东西的精神里洗净；他们从那些言论里、从耶稣本人身上遭遇的事情里，很快给自己造出规则和义务的诫命，对老师的自由效仿就变成了对主人的奴性服务。

en: What, then, is the contingent thing that occurs in Jesus' manner of acting and speaking and was capable of being taken for itself as something contingent, as something holy, and so of being venerated?
zh: 那么，在耶稣的行为方式和说话方式里出现、并且就其自身能够被当成偶然的东西、被当成神圣的东西、并这样受到崇敬的偶然东西，究竟是什么？

en: Since our intention is not to investigate how this or that positive doctrine came into Christianity or what changes have gradually taken place with it, etc.
zh: 因为我们的意图不是去考察这种或那种实证的学说怎样进入了基督教，或者它逐渐发生了哪些变化，等等。
